newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Barry Callebaut forecasts steady world cocoa price.
newsitem.headline: Barry Callebaut forecasts steady world cocoa price.

text.p: The chief executive officer of Barry Callebaut said on Thursday world cocoa prices should remain steady over the next year at around 1,000 stg a tonne.
The July LIFFE cocoa futures contract closed on Wednesday 23 stg down on the day at 994, breaking a key support level to reach a one-month low.
"I think the market is in balance. My view for the next 12 months is roughly stable. It could be a range of 1,000 stg, plus or minus five percent," Pierre Vermaut told reporters in a briefing.

He said that while production in top growers like the Ivory Coast, Ghana and Indonesia is steady or still increasing, the witches broom disease "has considerably reduced the output" in Malaysia and Brazil.
Consumption in Europe and North America, the world's leading consumers of chocolate products, will probably rise by one to two percent.
"I don't see any big swings" in prices, Vermaut said.

Barry Callebaut, the group formed by the merger of France's Cacao Barry and Swiss Callebaut AG, is the world's largest cocoa bean processor and a major force in the finished chocolate and chocolate coatings market. It operates 19 plants worldwide, including three cocoa bean processing plants in Ivory Coast.
